<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1283
Claimant:
Nicole Davis
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
2024-04-06
First notice of loss received from the insured's agent reporting a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road.
The claimant, a passenger in the insured's vehicle, reports a back strain and has retained counsel.
2024-04-29
Reviewed the policy file and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of loss.
No coverage issues identified at this stage.
2024-04-30
Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and describes the lane-change
impact consistent with the account given by the insured.
2024-06-03
Took recorded statements from the other driver and two independent witnesses. Each describes the sideswipe as it
was reported to us, with no material differences in sequence.
2024-06-24
Reviewed scene photographs and the damage estimate on both vehicles. The damage pattern lines up with the
described impact along the right rear quarter panel.
2024-07-03
Checked vehicle history and prior claim records. No earlier damage to this vehicle is on file, and nothing suggests the
damage predates the policy inception.
2024-07-16
Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the initial medical records. The claimant's account of the collision
matches what was given in earlier conversations with our office.
2024-07-31
Medical records show a lumbar strain diagnosed at urgent care. The injury is a typical outcome for a collision of this
type, and the records reference no prior treatment to the same body area.
2024-08-22
Received the treatment log from the provider. Care followed a usual course of physical therapy and tapeerd as the
claimant reported steady improvement in mobility and pain levels.
2024-09-05
Requested prior medical history through counsel. No earlier injury or complaint involving the same region of the back
appears in the records received to date.
2024-10-30
Reviewed the file with the handling supervisor. Liability and damage appear settled, the injury is consistent with the
mechanism, and the claim is moving to evaluation of the treatment cuorse and resolution.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
